title: Export rotation + checksum validation for scheduled customer usage dumps
creator: Ava Thompson
description: Reliable scheduled customer usage deliveries currently suffer from duplicate files, intermittent partial uploads, and noisy failed webhook deliveries. This ticket implements a coordinated export rotation + checksum manifest pattern and hardened webhook handshake to make CSV/S3 scheduled exports strongly-consistent and observable for customers. The goal is to ensure each scheduled export appears exactly once per run (or is clearly marked as partial), provide end-to-end integrity via checksums, and add backpressure-aware webhook delivery with exponential backoff + jitter and idempotency tokens.
acceptance_criteria: Each scheduled export run produces a manifest.json in the target S3 prefix containing file list, sizes, SHA256 checksums, export_epoch, and run_id
Upload semantics guarantee either a complete set of files + manifest or a 'partial' flag with reason; downstream consumers can detect and skip partial runs
S3 objects are written atomically by uploading to temp prefix and moving/renaming into final prefix (object copy/PutObject+Tagging) to avoid partial reads
Webhook deliveries include run_id and manifest URL and use idempotency-key header; retries follow exponential backoff with jitter and max 10 attempts
CSV schema versioning header present in each file, and Console shows export status (Succeeded/Partial/Failed) with checksum verification results
Monitoring: dashboard with per-customer export success rate, average time-to-finalize, checksum mismatch rate, and webhook delivery latency percentiles
E2E test covers a simulated partial upload, checksum mismatch detection, and webhook retry with idempotent consumer behavior
tasks: Design manifest schema (fields: run_id, export_epoch, files[{path,size,sha256}], status, started_at, finished_at, partial_reason)
Implement temp-prefix staging and atomic promotion for S3 exports in exports-service
Add SHA256 streaming checksum calculation in the CSV writer and include checksum in manifest
Extend scheduled-export controller to emit run_id and manifest URL to webhooks and Console events API
Implement webhook retry policy with idempotency-key and jittered exponential backoff in delivery-worker
Add Console backend endpoint to verify manifest checksums and mark run status; surface results in UI
Write integration tests: S3 staging, manifest validation, webhook retry and idempotency
Add observability: metrics (exports.run.success, exports.run.partial, exports.checksum.mismatch, webhook.retries), tracing and dashboard panels

2026-02-20 Diego Martinez: PoC for streaming SHA256 added to exports-service branch export-manifest-proto. Uses io.TeeReader equivalent; initial perf hit ~3% on 1M-row exports — acceptable baseline.

2026-02-25 Claire Nguyen (PM): Confirmed UX for 'partial' runs: Console will show yellow banner with reason and manifest link. Customer-facing docs PR in progress (confluence: /docs/exports/manifest-rfc).

2026-03-02 Diego Martinez: Implemented temp_prefix staging + S3 object tagging approach to mark 'complete'. Still validating cross-region copy semantics for dedicated customers in us-west-2 and eu-west-1.
2026-03-04 Security review request filed. Key items: ensure manifest URLs are signed and TTL-limited, restrict manifest reads to org role or presigned URL, and record KMS key usage in audit logs.

2026-03-06 Engineering review (PR #7842): Added idempotency-key to webhook headers; review note from Samir Patel: 'Add deterministic idempotency-key derivation from run_id+recipient_id and document collision possibilities.' Addressed in commit 9f2b.

2026-03-10 Diego Martinez: Integration test green on staging for single-run success and partial-run detection. Found a race in promotion step when multiple workers attempt promotion for same run — added distributed lock via redis:exports:run:{run_id}.

2026-03-10 QA note: Flaky test observed where checksum calculation differs due to CSV newline normalization between Linux/Windows producers. Decided to normalize to LF and include canonicalization step in writer. Added task to update customer docs about canonical CSV normalization.
resolution_notes: Promoted the staging implementation to canary on staging cluster 2026-03-10. Added redis-based run-level lock to prevent double promotion; canonicalized CSV newline behavior to LF to avoid checksum mismatches. Security review flagged manifest access TTLs — using presigned GET urls with 24h default. Remaining work: finalize S3 cross-region copy test matrix and add dedicated-customer IAM role documentation.
